analysis.conclusion: Null portalDocument emits the origin marker with no inline content; only its connected ownerDocument is acquired in layout. The subsequent render creates the mount in that Document before the first content root. The existing renderer-owned content and logical provider remain intact.

The attach effect remains dependent on shouldExist and portalDocument, and still attaches when an actual root exists. There is no new same-root shortcut. Deferring the first root until document acquisition avoids acquiring a view and then replacing its capabilities solely because the actual Document arrives.

An existing mount freezes the selected Document. Relevant origin or registry changes are still resolved against the current host and suspend its current material lease without moving the host. On retirement the existing refresh path clears the mount and Document; a later epoch reacquires the connected origin. Identity guards around release and reentrant resolution remain unchanged.

The state initializer no longer reads the ambient Document. The existing typeof document portal guard remains; origin resolution and connected projection remain layout work. Detached container creation and ref assignment in render pre-existed and are now deferred until the origin Document is known. No new connected-DOM render effect was found. This source review does not establish concurrent render abort or SSR/hydration runtime acceptance.
The change implements the existing draft Portal criteria without promoting their lifecycle, weakening admission, altering portable Prototype APIs, or changing material optical eligibility.
